title: URL Shortening Service (TinyURL)
question: Design a scalable URL shortener service like TinyURL. Walk through the read/write scale, encoding strategy, database schema, and caching layer.

rubric.name: requirements_capacity
rubric.description: Calculates read/write ratio (100:1), storage needs for 500M URLs/month, and URL length requirements (7 chars Base62).

rubric.name: encoding_generation_logic
rubric.description: Compares MD5/SHA256 truncation vs auto-increment ID + Base62 conversion or unique key generator service (KGS).

rubric.name: data_storage_decisions
rubric.description: Selects NoSQL key-value store (e.g. Cassandra or DynamoDB) or relational DB with clean indexing.

rubric.name: caching_scalability
rubric.description: Adds Redis caching layer following 80/20 hot URL rule and HTTP 301 vs 302 redirect trade-offs.

rubric.name: tradeoffs_failure_modes
rubric.description: Discusses 301 (Permanent, browser cached, less analytics) vs 302 (Temporary, hits server, trackable).

expected_signals: Explains Base62 encoding capability (62^7 = ~3.5 trillion URLs)
Addresses hash collision handling or uses a Key Generation Service (KGS)
Explains HTTP 301 (browser cache redirect) vs HTTP 302 (server hit for click analytics) trade-off
red_flags: Uses simple random hash without checking collisions
Fails to estimate storage or throughput numbers
Uses un-indexed relational table for high read traffic
follow_up_prompts: How would you prevent malicious users from spamming your system with millions of fake links?
If key analytics (click counts, geo, referrer) must be collected, how would you process them without slowing down the read path?
